rules: This is a production app used by real NYC drivers. Data correctness and notification reliability are the highest priorities — a wrong schedule or missed notification could cause a user to get a parking ticket.
Always use standalone Angular components (standalone: true). Never suggest or create NgModule-based patterns.
Use dayjs for all date manipulation. Never use native Date, moment, or date-fns.
Firestore queries belong in FeedService. Do not add Firestore calls directly to components.
Guard all Capacitor plugin calls with Capacitor.isNativePlatform() where the API does not exist in a browser.
Never change the Firebase App ID (com.cymbit.paras) — it is tied to App Store and Play Store listings.
Never run `firebase deploy` without explicit user confirmation.
Cloud Functions run on Node.js 18. Do not use Node 20+ APIs.
After any change to src/, remind the user to run `npx cap sync` to update native iOS and Android projects.
Bundle budget: 1.8 MB warning, 2 MB error. Flag new dependencies that could push the bundle over these limits.
Use inject() for dependency injection in Angular components and services, not constructor injection.
Prefer RxJS observables and AsyncPipe over async/await and stored properties in Angular components.
Use Spectator for all Angular tests. Never use TestBed.configureTestingModule directly.
Notification trigger times (7:30 AM today, 4 PM tomorrow) are user-configurable — never hardcode time logic without checking the notifications Firestore collection schema.
When suggesting a fix that affects Firestore collection/document structure, flag it explicitly — schema changes affect production data for all users.

Prevent god files: no single file should handle more than one clear responsibility. If a component, service, or function file exceeds ~200 lines or mixes concerns (e.g. UI logic + data fetching + auth + notifications in one class), split it. Services must be single-purpose — FeedService fetches feed data, AuthService handles auth, never combined. Flag any existing god file before adding more code to it and suggest how to split it instead.
